Before starting this sequence the teacher should check with the PPs the following prerequisites and prepare some activities to review and consolidate:
- Simple past (all forms).
- Adjectives (long / short syllables).
- Comparative (more / less).

## Past simple
Auxiliary: DO – **DID** – DONE
**Regular verbs (-ed)**
| |Base form|Past form|
|---|---|---|
|to|play|play**ed**|
|to|walk|walk**ed**|
|to|study|stud**ied**|
**Affirmative:** subject + base form + -ed
Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **played** football yesterday.

**Irregular verbs (different ways)**
| |Base form|Past form|
|---|---|---|
|to|make|made|
|to|ring|rang|
|to|go|went|
**Affirmative:** subject + 2nd form
Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **went** to the cinema.

**Negative:** subject + DIDN'T + base form
|Regular verbs:|Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **didn't play** football yesterday.|
|Irregular verbs:|Ex. I / you / he / she / it / we / they **didn't go** to the cinema last night.|

**Interrogative (Yes / No quest.):** DID + subject + base form ?
|Regular verbs:|Ex. **Did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **play** football yesterday?|
|Irregular verbs:|Ex. **Did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **go** to the cinema last night?|

**Interrogative (Wh- quest.):** Wh- word + DID + subject + base form ?
|Regular verbs:|Ex. **What did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **play** yesterday? **Football**|
|Irregular verbs:|Ex. **Where did** I / you / he / she / it / we / they **go** last night? **To the cinema**|

b:12.pre:
## Initial situation
> In the international “travel forum” of the tripadvisor.com website, you read a message of a tourist from England. He needs some information about Algeria. Think of some famous places you visited and write some information about them (famous landmarks, souks, old medinas, famous figures….). Turn this information into a travel brochure to be posted in the “travel forum”.
## I learn to integrate
> You have just returned from a three-day tour around Algeria.
> You want to post on your Facebook the report of this trip to make people around the world aware of the cultural and historical richness of your country Algeria, to know about the interesting places you visited.
> Describe your itinerary and give information about the places you visited (universal landmarks, old medinas, monuments, souks, fortresses…) and outstanding, famous figures in history, with a detailed map.
## Cross-curricular competencies
- Intel: The learner can understand verbal and nonverbal messages.
- Meth: He can work in groups.
- Com: He can lead a discussion. He can communicate appropriately. He can generate solutions to a problem.
- Per and soc: He can socialize through oral exchanges.
## Core values
- Valuing work in groups.
- Valuing world heritage.
- Openness to other cultures.
- Valuing travelling.
rows:
T greets his PPs. The PPs respond.

The teacher shows his PPs some pictures (or PowerPoint file) of some universal landmarks and places of interest in the world and starts a short discussion (to lead them to the situation). Example:
[[fig b:13 0.150 0.672 0.370 0.172]]

[[fig b:14 0.152 0.054 0.354 0.172]]
- Do you know these famous landmarks?
- Where are they situated?
- Can you locate them on the map?
- Why do people visit them?
- Do you know other monuments?
- Do you like travelling?
- Have you ever visited an interesting place (a landmark)?
- Can you give me information about it?
- What does a tourist prepare before starting his tour?
- Can you name some famous places (old medinas, souks, landmarks….) in your city (or region)?
- Are there any outstanding figures in history, literature or art in our region?

**Teacher writes the “initial situation” on the board. He reads it, then helps his PPs to interpret it.**

> In the international “travel forum” of the tripadvisor.com website, you read a message of a tourist from England. He needs some information about Algeria. Think of some famous places you visited and write some information about them (famous landmarks, souks, old medinas, famous figures….). Turn this information into a travel brochure to be posted in the “travel forum”.

**T invites his PPs to work in groups to discuss the problem and suggest solutions in 10 minutes.**
**The teacher invites his PPs to read what they wrote.**

**Using a spider graphic organizer, the teacher starts a discussion to introduce the topics of the new sequence.**

T: A group of Algerian middle school pupils are visiting London. They are riding an open-top double-decker bus and their English tourist guide is showing them London's most famous monuments and landmarks during this sightseeing tour.

Brainstorming / using prior knowledge

## The 1st listening
Teacher invites his PPs to listen to the tourist guide talking to sightseers and choose the right answer:
a) The tourists are going on a sightseeing tour around: 1- London 2- Liverpool 3- Manchester

c) The Westminster Palace was built in the ………… century: 1- tenth 2- eleventh 3- twelfth
## The 2nd listening
The Ls listen again to the English tourist guide part 1 and work with partners. They compare their answers then correct each other.
## The 3rd listening
Listen to the tourist guide talking to the PPs and find the missing words (task 2 page 11).

To listen and choose the right answer

The teacher greets his PPs / the PPs respond.
The teacher pins on the board some flashcards of famous monuments and asks his PPs to find their names.

The teacher shows his PPs a flash card of the Eiffel Tower and invites them to say what they know about it.
[[fig b:21 0.155 0.659 0.247 0.166]]

Teacher writes on the board the following note about the Eiffel Tower then asks some guiding questions:
> The Eiffel Tower is the most famous monument of France. It is situated in Paris. It was designed by Gustave Eiffel. It was built by 250 workers. It was constructed between 1887 and 1889 for the Exposition of Paris.
- Where is the Eiffel Tower situated?
- Who designed it?
- Who built it?
- When? And why?

T: Now read the following sentences and compare them:
A) Gustave Eiffel designed the Eiffel Tower.
B) The Eiffel Tower was designed by Gustave Eiffel.

T **draws the Ls' attention and asks some guiding questions:**
- Underline the verbs in sentences A and B. What do you remark? What is the difference?
- Underline the subjects.
- What happened to the subject and the verb in sentence B?
- What about the object?
[[fig b:22 0.152 0.623 0.380 0.052]]
So, sentence A is in active form (the subject does the action).
Sentence B is in passive form (when the object of the active sentence becomes the subject and the verb becomes “was + past participle”, we call it passive form).

**Grammar tool:**
T highlights rules of passive voice (pages 30/31).

Introduce the target language in a context

Giving the opportunity to the learners to guess and elicit the new structure

## Reinforce and consolidate
**Activity one: Underline the correct variant:**
1. I am helped / was helped yesterday.
2. Milk is bought / was bought every day.
3. Nick is sent / was sent to the library yesterday.
4. Liz was given / were given a new toy last night.
5. This story is published / was published 2 years ago.
6. Milk is delivered / was delivered every day.
7. The cars are bought / were bought last year.
8. My sisters was invited / were invited to the party last week.

**Activity two: Rewrite the sentences in the Passive Voice:**
1. We bought this car yesterday.
2. W. Shakespeare wrote “Romeo and Juliet”.
3. I made the report last week.
4. We designed a nice plan.

**Activity three: The Statue of Liberty**
Complete the sentences (Active or Passive Voice). You must either use Simple Present or Simple Past.
1. The Statue of Liberty (give) ………… to the United States by France.
2. It (be) ………… a present on the 100th anniversary of the United States.
3. The Statue of Liberty (design) ………… by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi.
4. It (complete) ………… in France in July 1884.
5. In 350 pieces, the statue then (ship) ………… to New York, where it (arrive) ………… on 17 June 1885.
6. The pieces (put) ………… together and the opening ceremony (take) ………… place on 28 October 1886.
7. The Statue of Liberty (be) ………… 46 m high (93 m including the base).
8. The statue (represent) ………… the goddess of liberty.
9. She (hold) ………… a torch in her right hand and a tablet in her left hand.
10. On the tablet you (see / can) ………… the date of the Declaration of Independence (July 4, 1776).
11. Every year, the Statue of Liberty (visit) ………… by many people from all over the world.

- No, I didn't enjoy my weekend because I was ill.

The teacher, using a cause and effect graphic organizer, elicits and introduces the new target language in a context.
|Cause|Effects|
|---|---|
|I was ill|Effect 1: I didn't go outside|
| |Effect 2: I didn't use my bicycle|
| |Effect 3: ……………|
| |Effect 4 – Effect 5 – Effect 6|

|As|he was ill,|he didn't go outside.|
|---|---|---|
|connector of reason|cause|effect|
Now find the cause, the effect and the connector in the following sentence.
|He was ill,|so|he didn't use his bicycle.|
|---|---|---|
|cause|connector of effects|effect|

Teacher: We often use ==as== and ==because==, ……….. when we want to focus more on the causes and the reasons…
We often use ==so== and ==therefore==, ……… when we want to focus more on the results (consequences).

The teacher greets his PPs / the PPs respond.

T asks some questions:

- How many vowels do we have? What are they?
- How many consonants do we have?

Recall and use prior knowledge

Paving the way

The teacher shows his PPs some flashcards about the Blue Mosque of Turkey and sees if they know its location.
[[fig b:50 0.156 0.743 0.462 0.205]]
T writes on the board a note about this mosque and invites his PPs to read it.
> The ==bl==ue mosque of Istanbul is a ==spl==endid la==ndm==ark. It is bui==lt== between 1609 and 1616. A lot of touri==sts== ==fr==om all over the wo==rld== come to visit this ==pl==ace.
**Guiding questions:**
Teacher asks students to consider the underlined consonants:
==bl==ue – ==spl==endid – la==ndm==ark – bui==lt== – touri==sts== – ==pl==ace
T: Is there any vowel between these consonants?
T: When we have two or more consonants without a vowel between them we call them a ‘cluster’.

Present the target sounds in a context

Giving the opportunity to the learners to analyse the target sounds

! Highlighting rules about what a cluster is and when it can occur: My pronunciation tools page 27.

**Task one:** The PPs are invited to listen and identify consonant clusters in each of the following words (Task 12 page 30).
**Task two:**
The learners are invited to listen and identify the position (initial or final) of the clusters in Task 1.
**Task three:** Circle the consonant clusters in the following text:
> The Great Mosque (Jamaa el-Kebir) is the oldest of Algiers' mosques. An inscription inside shows that the building existed as far back as the 11th century, although it has to be said that the mosque has been much altered since then. The minaret is said to be the work of the Sultan of Tlemcen in the 14th century.

Highlighting rules about consonant clusters

To recognize the consonant clusters (cc)

Check and reinforce

**Task 4:**
In groups, the PPs prepare sheets (or cards) and write on each one a word that contains a cluster they knew before. After that, the groups show their cards to their classmates. The group who makes a correct word wins a point. At the end, the group with the most points is the winner.
The correct cards can be displayed on the wall.
